turns.t: Good morning, doctor. I'm sure it's nothing, but my partner thinks I should talk to someone, because I've been all over the place with my moods.
Thank you for coming. What has your partner noticed? ~
That I'm up and down. I can be flying on Monday, full of plans, and then flat by Thursday. And I snap more than I used to. ~
Do you feel low at all, when you're flat?
Flat, not low. No, I wouldn't say low. I don't feel sad.
Any thoughts of harming yourself, or of life not being worth it?
No, not at all.
When you're up, do you sleep much less, or feel your thoughts racing?
I sleep a bit less, perhaps. But not racing. No, nothing like that.
How's work?
I'm a marketing manager. It's been crazy, a big launch, sixty-hour weeks.
Do you drink, smoke, anything else?
I drink a bit at weekends, a few glasses of wine, and I'm trying to cut down on coffee.
And do you exercise?
I run three times a week, when I'm not too tired.
Any history of mental health problems, past or present?
I had anxiety at university, and an episode of low mood in my twenties after a break-up. That's all.
Let me check you over. Pulse and blood pressure. ~
Go ahead. ~
Pulse 74, blood pressure 118 over 74, temperature 36.6, oxygen 99 percent.
Fine? ~
Fine. Any breathlessness or palpitations when you're up, any heat intolerance?
No, none.
Hold your hands out. ~
Like this? ~
Steady, no tremor. And you're making good eye contact, and you speak calmly and clearly.
Do I sound mad? ~
Not at all. You sound like someone who's very busy, and tired. ~
That's about right. ~
Sixty-hour weeks, less sleep, and alcohol can all make moods swing without it being a mental illness. ~
That's reassuring, actually. ~
I'm not dismissing it. Keep a mood diary for a month, with your sleep, caffeine and alcohol.
My partner will love that. ~
Aim for a regular bedtime, and keep the wine for one or two evenings.
Understood. ~
If you start to feel very high, can't sleep at all for several days, or feel low or hopeless, ring us at once.
I will. Thank you. ~

chief_complaint.value: I've been all over the place with my moods

physical_examination.normalized_finding: Good eye contact, calm clear speech

clinical_actions.description: Keep a one-month mood diary with sleep, caffeine and alcohol
Regular bedtime and limit wine to one or two evenings
Ring at once if very high with no sleep for days, or low or hopeless
